req.title: Register form html served
req.statement: The system shall include HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password' in the /auth/register page.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the /auth/register page should serve an HTML form with 'username' and 'password' fields. This is a functional requirement that can be tested by verifying the presence of these fields in the HTML response. We will use Equivalence Partitioning (EP) to test a typical case, Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) to test edge cases, and Negative Path (NEG) to ensure proper error handling.

tests.name: test_register_form_html_served_positive
preconditions: The Flask application is running in test mode.
actions: Send a GET request to the /auth/register endpoint.
expected: The response contains HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password'.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/auth/register')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'<input name="username"' in r.data
assert b'<input name="password"' in r.data

tests.name: test_register_form_html_served_boundary
preconditions: The Flask application is running in test mode.
actions: Send a GET request to the /auth/register endpoint with a large query string.
expected: The response contains HTML input fields named 'username' and 'password'.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
query_string = '?' + 'a' * 2048
r = client.get('/auth/register' + query_string)
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'<input name="username"' in r.data
assert b'<input name="password"' in r.data
